result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and parallel on-street parking. While the street environment appears low-speed, the lack of marked crossings and the visual obstructions created by parked vehicles present risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on both sides of the street, including a large Jeep, block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks or pedestrian signage may lead to unpredictable crossing behavior in a residential area.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or potential crossing points to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to corners.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a sidewalk that is interrupted by a wide, paved alleyway serving multiple garages. This creates a significant conflict zone where pedestrians must cross a vehicle path without clear priority or continuous infrastructure.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Alley Entrance
hazards.description: A wide, paved alleyway creates a large gap in the sidewalk where vehicles cross the pedestrian path without clear markings or priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the sidewalk ends and the paved alley begins.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The building corner and parked vehicles may obstruct the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers exiting the alley.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the alley entrance, near the brick building and parked silver car.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Treatment
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk material and level across the alley entrance to reinforce pedestrian priority and slow entering/exiting vehicles.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Alley Entrance
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the alley entrance to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and mature street trees providing a buffer from traffic. While the narrow roadway naturally encourages lower speeds, the high density of parked cars creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross mid-block.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street creates a 'screen' effect, making it difficult for drivers to see pedestrians, especially children, who might step into the roadway from between vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight and reduce the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to intersections or mid-block crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Cushions
interventions.description: Install speed cushions to maintain low vehicle speeds on this residential corridor.
